Where it began

Ishant Sharma was born in Delhi on 2 September 1988, and it was for Delhi that he played his domestic cricket. He toured England with India's Under-19 side in 2006 and Pakistan in 2006–07, playing three youth Tests along the way.

He was only 18 when the senior selectors first called his name, for a tour of South Africa, although that trip did not happen for him in the end. His chance came instead in Bangladesh in May 2007, where his first Test spell was a tidy three overs for five runs.

The player

Australia saw the best of him early. On India's tour there that winter, at Perth, a fine spell at Ricky Ponting ended with the Australian captain's wicket and helped India to victory. Later that year, at home against the same opponents, he took 16 wickets, more than anyone else, and he was named player of the series as India won it 2–0. No Indian fast bowler had won that award in a home Test series since Kapil Dev in 1983. Over six Tests he dismissed Ponting six times.

His career ran from 2007 to 2021: 105 Tests, 311 wickets at 32.41, with 11 five-wicket hauls and one ten-wicket match. The best of them was 7 for 74 at Lord's in 2014, a spell that bowled India to a 95-run win.

What made him special

Standing 6 ft 4 in, he was quick when he wanted to be, topping 152 km/h in 2008, but over the years he became a bowler of rhythm and control who would run in all day. In 2011 he was the fifth-youngest man to reach 100 Test wickets, and in the West Indies that year he took 22 wickets at 16.86 in the series. In February 2021 at Motera he played his 100th Test, joining Kapil Dev as only the second Indian fast bowler to get there.

The bat was a slower story. He averaged 8.27, and his maiden Test fifty waited until 2019 in the West Indies, batting at nine. Yet in 2010 at Mohali he made 31 alongside VVS Laxman in a partnership of 81 as India won by one wicket, and nobody in the dressing room was counting the average that day.

Away from the middle

He was in the India side that won the 2013 Champions Trophy, and in 2020 he received the Arjuna Award. In 2018 he spent two months with Sussex, the 9th Indian to play for the county. His IPL travels took in Kolkata Knight Riders, Deccan Chargers, Kings XI Punjab and Delhi Capitals, and in 2026 he was in the Gujarat Titans squad that reached the final. In 2016 he married the Indian basketball player Pratima Singh.

And finally

In England in 2018 he drew level with Kapil Dev for the most Test wickets by an Indian bowler in that country. As for Alastair Cook, who took one Test wicket in his whole career, the batsman he got out was Ishant. Every fast bowler likes to give a little something back.
